item.title: leafOfTree/WindowTabs
item.description:
A utility that brings browser-style tabbed window management to the desktop.

WindowTabs

Browser-style tabs for your desktop windows. Group windows from any apps and switch between them with a click or a shortcut.

Important

v2026.11.05-beta.1 preview: mouse gestures, a group editor, clearer tab colours, close buttons on the active tab only or never, icons-only groups by default, and tab shortcuts that step aside where they cannot act. What's changed →

Get started

Download WindowTabs.exe from Releases and run it. It runs in the system tray.

  • Group windows: drag a tab onto another window's tab bar. Drag it away to ungroup.
  • Group an app automatically: right-click its tab → Enable auto-grouping.
  • Put the tabs where you like: hold the right mouse button on a tab and drag the tabs along the window's edge, across the top or down the side. New windows of that app start there; Align tabs in the tab menu puts them back.
  • Run any command or change any setting: press Ctrl + Alt + P and type its name (see Command palette).
  • Settings: right-click a tab or the tray icon.

Grouped windows move and resize together. Tabs hide on maximized windows; point at the top edge to show them, or set Auto-hide tabs to Never.

Shortcuts

Action Default
Next / previous tab Ctrl + Alt + → / ←
Tab 1–9 Ctrl + 1–9 (or Alt)
Search tabs Ctrl + Alt + T; Alt + Enter on a window gives it a key of its own
New window of the current app Ctrl + Alt + N
Switch tabs with the mouse Scroll over the tab bar, or Shift + scroll over the window
Move the current tab Ctrl + scroll over the tab bar
Close a tab Ctrl + Alt + W, or middle-click

Change any shortcut under Settings → Shortcuts. If Ctrl/Alt + number conflicts with an app, turn it off for that app from the tab's right-click menu.

Optional, off by default: switch on hover, a picture of a tab's window when the pointer rests on it, a leader key to pick tabs by letter (Alt + F, then the key on the tab), automatic tab colors, and an Alt+Tab replacement.

Drag files onto a tab and pause to bring that window forward. On a File Explorer tab, let go to drop them into its folder as Explorer would: Ctrl copies, Shift moves, right-drag asks, and Ctrl + Z in Explorer undoes it.

Features

  • Appearance: light, dark or follow Windows; Joined, Folder or Floating tabs; per-tab, per-app or per-group colors.
  • Pinned tabs: right-click a tab → Pin to keep it at the front of its group, out of reach of Close others, Close tabs to the right and Close all, across restarts.
  • App rules: choose which running apps get tabs and which group automatically. Under Groups across apps, add groups so windows of different apps join one group; an app's menu there takes only the windows whose title, window class or command line matches, as for apps that run under pythonw.exe or java.exe. Groups made by dragging tabs are remembered and listed in a panel of their own below. Either kind of group can keep a color: right-click a tab → Tab color → Remember color for this group, and every tab in the group takes it.
  • Split view: show two or more of a group's windows side by side or stacked, as in a browser or editor. Right-click a tab → Split view and pick a window for each side, or drag a tab to a window's edge. Drag the bar between the panes to resize them, right-click it to swap, equalize, switch direction or end the split. Shortcuts for a window on the right or below and for moving the focus between panes are under Settings → Shortcuts, unset by default.
  • Group editor: Edit groups… in the palette shows every group as a row of tabs, with the loose windows below. Drag tabs between rows, onto a window to split it, or onto New group; nothing moves until Save.
  • Workspaces: save groups and window positions, then restore them onto open windows; apps that are not running can be launched and their windows restored. Shortcuts to save one and to restore the last saved or restored one are under Settings → Shortcuts, unset by default.
  • Mouse gestures: turn them on under Settings → Gestures, then hold the right button and drag, such as up then right for the next tab. A gesture runs a WindowTabs command or sends a shortcut to the window, and an app can have its own: browsers and File Explorer start with back, forward and the like. A right click without dragging still opens the app's menu.
  • Taskbar: optionally combine each group into one taskbar button, which shows every app in the group.
  • Languages: English, 中文, 日本語, العربية.

Command palette and command line

Ctrl + Alt + P opens the command palette: type a command's name and press Enter. Every tab menu action, split view command, workspace command and setting is there, with its shortcut beside it. A setting that is on or off shows a switch and is turned in place; a choice is picked from its list, a size typed and saved as you type, a colour picked, and anything else opens the settings window on it. Restore workspace… lists the saved workspaces. Alt + Enter on an action sets its shortcut, as Settings → Shortcuts does; a setting's shortcut opens the palette on its choices or its box. The window search (Ctrl + Alt + T) is a box of its own, over the group's tabs or every window.

Searching works the same in both boxes:

  • Type words in any order; each can be part of a name, an app or a word a command is known by, so color tab finds Tab color… and merge finds Group this app.
  • Leave out the spaces, or type the first letters of the words: movedown or md finds Move down the list. These come after rows that have the words themselves.
  • Type a shortcut, starting with its modifier or function key, such as ctrl+alt+t or f5, to see which command or window has it.
  • The last search and recently used actions come first.
  • ↑ / ↓ and Page Up / Page Down move, Enter runs, Esc goes back or closes, Tab goes round the window search's scopes, Ctrl + U clears what is typed and Ctrl + Backspace deletes a word.

The same commands run from a command line, in the running WindowTabs:

WindowTabs.exe --command next-tab
WindowTabs.exe --command tab-color Blue
WindowTabs.exe --workspace "Project A"
WindowTabs.exe --group "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" notepad.exe
WindowTabs.exe --commands

--group starts the programs and puts the windows they open into one group, and --workspace restores a saved workspace; either also starts WindowTabs when it is not running. --commands lists every command with its id.

Settings and updates

Settings save automatically to %AppData%\WindowTabs\WindowTabsSettings.json. For portable use, put that file next to WindowTabs.exe. Export, import and reset are under Settings → Support.

To update, exit WindowTabs from the tray and replace the exe. Settings are kept.

Troubleshooting

  • No tabs on a window? Check Settings → App rules. Dialogs don't get tabs.
  • Odd behavior after upgrading? Settings → Support → Reset to defaults (your old settings are backed up first).
  • Run as administrator? Not needed and not recommended. Windows blocks some input between admin and normal windows, and groups of normal windows keep a taskbar button each even with Combine taskbar icons on; the group's tab menu says why.
  • Dropping files on a tab does nothing? Windows blocks dragging from an app into one running as administrator.

Still stuck? Open an issue and paste the troubleshooting report from Settings → Support. It leaves out window titles and paths.

Development

Build and run

WindowTabs is an F# WinForms app on .NET Framework 4.8, with a small C# project for Win32 interop. To build on Windows 10 or 11:

1. Install the tools

  • .NET 10.0 SDK: choose the Windows SDK installer (usually x64).
  • .NET Framework 4.8 Developer Pack: the runtime alone is not enough to build.

2. Download, build and run

Open a new PowerShell window in the folder where you want to keep the source:

git clone https://github.com/leafOfTree/WindowTabs
cd WindowTabs
dotnet build WindowTabs.sln                 # Debug: WtProgram\bin\Debug\WindowTabs.exe
dotnet build WindowTabs.sln -c Release      # Release: WtProgram\bin\Release\WindowTabs.exe (single exe)

The first build downloads NuGet dependencies and needs internet access. Run the generated exe to start WindowTabs in the system tray; exit it before rebuilding, as the running exe locks the output. If dotnet is not found, reopen PowerShell after installation.

Alternatively, use Visual Studio

Install Visual Studio 2026, select the .NET desktop development workload, and keep its default recommended components. Open WindowTabs.sln, set WtProgram as the startup project, and press F5.

AI-assisted contributions are welcome. Make sure you understand and have tested your changes. See AGENTS.md, architecture and testing.

Things to know before changing code

  • Threads: each tab group runs on its own UI thread, and the main thread owns settings and window discovery. Calls between them go through the adapters in Shared/Services.fs. Read architecture before touching this.
  • UI text: every visible string lives in Shared/Strings.fs with English, Chinese and Japanese. Machine translation is fine for a first draft; native speakers can refine it.
  • Settings: names, defaults and ranges are declared once in Shared/SettingsCatalog.fs; the Settings window, search and reset all read from it.
  • DPI and themes: use logical pixels and scale with Dpi.scale; check your UI in light, dark and high-contrast modes.

Code signing policy

Free code signing provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation.

  • Committers and reviewers: contributors
  • Approvers: @leafOfTree

Release binaries are built from source by GitHub Actions (release.yml), and every signing request is approved by a maintainer. AI coding agents assist with development, but all changes are reviewed and merged by a human maintainer.

Privacy policy

This program will not transfer any information to other networked systems unless specifically requested by the user or the person installing or operating it.

Credits and license
